items.text: COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.lawCode: Amd Part C Subpart H §1, Chap 20 of 2015
items.lawSection: New York State Urban Development Corporation Act
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8235

SPONSOR: FLANAGAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend subpart H of part C of chapter 20 of
the laws of 2015, relating to appropriating money for certain municipal
corporations and school districts, in relation to authorizing funds in
the case of certain tax certiorari challenges or agreed upon settle-
ments; and to permit certain boards of education to establish a tax
certiorari stabilization reserve fund

 
PURPOSE:

To allow municipalities and school districts that either face judgments
or agree to settlements with LIPA from its tax certiorari challenges to
access the electric generating facility cessation mitigation program and
to allow the school districts that would be impacted by any judgment or
settlement between the municipalities and LIPA to receive funds from the
same program.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Section 1 opens up the electric generating facility cessation
mitigation program to local government entities that, on or after April
1, 2018, lose a tax certiorari challenge with LIPA or settle with LIPA
such that the local government entity sees a reduction of the facility's
real property taxes or PILOTs decreases by 20% or more. For local
government entities that are eligible per a tax certiorari proceeding
brought by LIPA, they would be able to access the funds for 15 years.

Section 2: Section 2 allows the Port Jefferson, Northport-East North-
port, North Shore, and Island Park school districts to establish tax
certiorari stabilization reserve funds, and specifically points out that
these school districts would be eligible to receive funds from the elec-
tric generating facility cessation mitigation fund.

Section 3: Section 4 sets forth an immediate effective date; provided
however, that the amendments to section 1 of subpart H of part C of
chapter 20 of the laws of 2015 made by section one of this act shall not
affect the repeal of such subpart and shall be deemed repealed there-
with.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 2010, the Long Island Power Authority ("LIPA") initiated tax certior-
ari proceedings on its four legacy power plants. Over the last eight
years, LIPA and the respective assessing municipalities-Nassau County,
Huntington Town, Brookhaven Town, and the Village of Port Jefferson-have
been engaged in long standing litigation on the tax certiorari chal-
lenges, including in some cases whether LIPA had the right to bring the
challenges in the first place.

Due to the significant costs associated with these challenges, many
attempts have been made by the municipalities and LIPA to settle their
individual litigations. Whether or not a settlement can be reached in
each case is a determination for each local municipality to make, as is
the decision to go to trial or not.

Whatever decision each municipality decides, this legislation is crit-
ical to providing these municipalities-and the school districts who are
not parties to the litigation but would likely face the harshest impacts
of any settlement or adverse judgment-with access to the Electric Gener-
ating Facility Cessation Mitigation Fund ("EGFCM Fund"). The EGFCM Fund
was established to help mitigate the loss of property taxes or PILOTs on
electric generating facilities that close down, creating economic hard-
ships for communities and school districts that have relied on those
incoming funds for years or decades. This legislation needs to be
expanded because a settlement, even a long term settlement, or in the
worst case scenario a successful LIPA challenge in court, could have
lasting financial impacts on the communities and school districts in
which the plants are located. By opening up this existing fund, it will
help alleviate any potential reductions in property taxes or PILOTs paid
by the plants going forward.

Additionally, this legislation would ensure that the school districts
have a dedicated mechanism to receive money from the EGFCM Fund through
a tax certiorari stabilization reserve fund.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

No new cost to the state. The appropriation provided for in this bill
was allocated in the 2018-2019 Enacted Budget.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately; provided however, that the
amendments to section 1 of subpart H of part C of chapter 20 of the laws
of 2015 made by section one of this act shall not affect the repeal of
such subpart and shall be deemed repealed therewith.

summary: Authorizes funds to municipalities from the UDC in the case of certain tax certiorari challenges or agreed upon settlements resulting in loss of tax revenues or increased tax levies of over twenty percent or in regards to a settlement agreement, a reduction in real property taxes or a payment in lieu of taxes of at least twenty percent in the aggregate over the term of such settlement agreement; and permits the establishment of tax certiorari stabilization reserve funds.
